[{"deploy":{"id":"dep-daauu9navr4c738klj3g","commit":{"id":"c15d0ddb591672d308b02d585819a9295a62ecf4","message":"deploy: wire the release-verification workflow

Every push to staging or main now ends with the Deploy role proving what the
deploy actually produced: the expected commit serving, the public URL
answering over valid TLS with this site's content marker, custom domains
verified, live Render configuration matching render.yaml. Healthy staging
deploys end in a staging->main promotion PR assembled with evidence; failed
production deploys end in a rollback to the last known-good deploy. The agent
writes the release record, the workflow commits it — same division as the QA
verdict — and paths-ignore on pipeline/releases keeps that commit from
re-triggering verification of its own content-identical rebuild.

Per-repo values live in pipeline/deploy.config.json so deploy.yml itself is
parity-identical across repos. Skips with a notice until RENDER_API_KEY and
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY are both configured; Render offers no read-only keys, so
the charter's hard limits and a tool allowlist without git push or gh pr
merge are the fence.

Wiring this exposed two subset gaps: the validator ignored pipeline/releases
entirely, and the release-record schema leaned on 'not' and a bare
required-only if-clause, neither of which the deliberately minimal validator
implements — rules that would have silently stopped existing. The validator
now scans release records, the schema is rewritten inside the supported
subset, and its header now warns that an ignored keyword is a rule that
silently stopped existing. Verified with fixtures: a clean record passes;
recorded drift, a failed deploy status, and a rollback on a staging success
each fail on the right rule.
